stories.headline: Russian strikes hit two Kyiv bridges and disrupt utilities as Ukraine holds talks with US and European representatives

sources.body:
Two major bridges in the Ukrainian capital have reportedly been struck in a Russian ballistic missile attack, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

The missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges spanning the Dnipro River, Klitschko said, adding that water and power supplies in the city had been disrupted.

Meanwhile, Ukraine struck the landmark Kerch Bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea for a second consecutive day, the region's Moscow-installed governor said.

President Volodymyr Zelensky had earlier warned that Moscow might launch further strikes on the country on Monday night, after Ukrainian, US and European officials held further talks aimed at ending the years-long conflict.

Those online talks, attended by US envoy Jared Kushner and US special envoy Steve Witkoff, came after Russia said it recorded the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began.

Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems".

"Some areas are experiencing disruptions to water and heating supplies", he added.

Some of Kyiv's above-ground subway services have been damaged in the overnight attacks, officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.

Residents of Kyiv typically shelter in the city's underground stations during air raids.

Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv. An estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.

Several of the capital's major bridges were also targeted by Russian drone strikes in October .

Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkast region, according to local officials.

Separately, the Ukrainian military struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea again overnight , the region's Moscow-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov said on Telegram.

Traffic across the bridge had been suspended, he added.

The landmark bridge, which has come under repeated attack by Ukrainian forces, was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014.

Russian President Vladimir Putin inaugurated the bridge to great fanfare in 2018. The severity of the latest strike on Kerch Bridge is still unclear, though it is protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.

Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards the capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said.

The latest round of tit-for-tat strikes came after US, Ukrainian and European officials held talks on ways to facilitate "direct engagement" between Russia and Europe to end the war.

Following Monday's meeting, US envoy Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law, said the US was committed to providing Ukraine with a "strong, credible security guarantees", as well as a path towards EU membership.

He added that Nato "will remain a critical pillar of European security", and that preparations are underway for a further multilateral meeting "in the near future".
sources.headline: Two major Kyiv bridges hit in Russian attack, mayor says

sources.body: Russian forces struck two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks came as Moscow launched a wider wave of drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, including in the regions of Cherkasy and Kharkiv.
sources.headline: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies

sources.body:
Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee said there had been ‘no change in Russia’s position’ as Russia and Ukraine strike major infrastructure.

Ukraine has held new talks with United States and European officials on ending the war with Russia, hours before Kyiv’s mayor reported strikes on two bridges in the capital.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described Monday’s online discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European representatives as “not easy”. But he said participants had agreed to meet in Berlin with the “Coalition of the Willing”, a group of countries supporting Ukraine, as the US and Europe step up peace talks this week.

“Diplomatic processes are actively underway and we hope that these efforts will not be in vain,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly address.

He also warned that Ukrainian intelligence indicated Russia was preparing major strikes that night and throughout Tuesday.

Later on Monday, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said preliminary reports indicated that the North and South bridges across the Dnipro River had been hit. Air defence units were operating, and Reuters news agency witnesses heard a series of loud explosions.

Ukraine on Monday struck a key bridge and targeted oil refineries in what Russian defence ministry data indicated was the biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of full-scale war in 2022. The Crimea Bridge was again struck overnight, with nearly 200 drones intercepted near Moscow, according to Telegram statements.

Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, said Washington was making progress towards an agreement in coordination with Russia, Ukraine and Europe.

“Important challenges remain, and a final agreement will require difficult decisions,” he wrote on X.

He said he and Witkoff had also spoken with Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov about the next steps. Their discussions included how to arrange direct engagement between Europe and Russia so each could hear the other’s concerns and proposals.

The exchanges followed last week’s talks in Abu Dhabi , where US, Ukrainian and Russian officials met together for the first time in nine months. Those negotiations produced an agreement on a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on ending the war.

Witkoff and Kushner later met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and said European representatives would join the next round. On Monday, Moscow disputed that assertion.

Zelenskyy said representatives from France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland had participated fully in Monday’s discussion and would have the same representation in future meetings with Russian negotiators.

Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to expand the talks beyond the existing Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations. No date had been agreed for the next round, he added.

European governments, meanwhile, were preparing their negotiating team while maintaining pressure on Moscow.

Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee welcomed renewed talks and the agreement on EU representation following diplomatic meetings in Abu Dhabi and Dublin last week. But she said, “Russia has clearly not changed its position.”
sources.headline: Ukraine holds peace talks with US, Europe as conflict escalates

stories.headline: Five EU countries announce plans for a migrant deportation hub in Rwanda

sources.body:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”.

Officials hope to send 100 people to Rwanda from early next year to test the model. The scheme will apply to adults whose claims to asylum have been rejected or others with no legal right to live in the EU.

In theory, according to diplomatic sources, migrants would stay in a reception centre in Rwanda for a couple of months, before choosing to integrate into life in the Great Lakes country or return to their home nation.

Unlike the failed scheme pursued by the British Conservative government in Rwanda, or Italy’s agreement with Albania , it will not apply to people pursuing asylum claims.

The reception centre, which would be an open facility, was not intended to house people long term but to accommodate regular flows of people, the countries said. Diplomatic sources said the EU countries were not using British-funded facilities built in Kigali.

The governments involved argue it will protect the European asylum system while removing the incentive for irregular migrants to come to Europe .

Denmark’s immigration minister, Morten Bødskov, whose government has pioneered a tough line on migration widely emulated across the EU, said it was “a huge breakthrough”.

The German interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, said: “Return hubs offer a positive approach for people without the right to stay and with no prospects in Europe, whose countries of origin do not cooperate in the repatriation process.”

Andy Burnham told reporters last week that the UK had not had direct discussions with European governments involved in return hubs but “we will watch that with interest, learning from what went on in the past. The public want us to do whatever we can to deal with illegal immigration.”

Critics have highlighted the ethical difficulties of striking an agreement with Rwanda’s repressive government , which was found in 2024 by the US state department to allow state security forces and civilian officials to commit human rights abuses with impunity, while also raising concerns about freedom of expression and forced labour.

Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, said on Monday the move had no “future or humanity”. “I don’t see any future or humanity in that. It’s not the solution,” Sanchez, an outspoken defender of immigration in a Europe that has tilted to the right in recent years, told Telecinco television.
sources.headline: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

sources.body: Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark on Monday unveiled a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda -- the first such facility outside the bloc. The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
sources.headline: EU nations unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub

sources.body:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 .

Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.

"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.

The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.

Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.

The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".
sources.headline: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda

stories.headline: Trump heads to Asia for planned nuclear and Ukraine talks with Xi and Putin

sources.body: US President Donald Trump headed to Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. Trump also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.
sources.headline: Trump heads to Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia

sources.body:
Experts say US president may lean toward global affairs after domestic influence curtailed in midterm elections

Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.

The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.

At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand , push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.

He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.

White House officials said the president would be accompanied to Apec by Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX entrepreneur who spent almost $500m (£380m) unsuccessfully supporting Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.

The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from the Nvidia spying scandal , which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.

The US president has said he does not plan to bring up the subject ; administration officials insist he will not do so and that the meeting will be dedicated to implementing a trade agreement between the two superpowers.

Huang persuaded the Trump administration to lift restrictions on the sale of Nvidia’s AI chips to China that had been imposed during Joe Biden’s presidency.

Mao Ning, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, told reporters on Monday that at the trilateral summit, Xi, Trump and Putin “will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance”.

Some analysts have characterised the meeting as a “big three” gathering echoing the 1945 Yalta meeting of Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin that in effect carved up postwar Europe, between a communist-ruled east and a democratic, capitalist west.

Such a prospect has alarmed Ukraine , which fears that Putin – who initially suggested the trilateral meeting – will use it to persuade Trump and Xi to agree to a settlement of the war with Russia on Moscow’s terms.

However, Trump has said Ukraine will not be up for debate at the meeting and that its main purpose will be to discuss ending the US’s war with Iran and “denuclearisation” – shorthand for a deal among the three powers to limit nuclear arms.
sources.headline: Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term

stories.headline: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East amid renewed tensions with Iran

sources.body:
The US president oscillates between strike threats on Iran and insisting the war ‘militarily is effectively over’

A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.

The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September. It joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian shipping.

The George HW Bush arrived in the region in April, while the George Washington arrived in August. The navy previously had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East in April, for the first time since 2003.

In addition to the three aircraft carriers, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship, according to the navy. Two more destroyers are in the Red Sea.

The Roosevelt had deployed along with the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group, which includes the USS John P Murtha and USS Anchorage amphibious landing ships and around 2,000 marines. Those ships have yet to make it to the region.

The third carrier arrived nearly two weeks after midterm elections that saw voters deliver major losses to Trump’s Republican party, driven in part by the unpopularity of the Iran war and its economic effects. The results led JD Vance to publicly break with Trump over the conflict, posting on social media that “the reason we lost is the war”.

Trump has insisted it was the right thing to do and has not ruled out restarting the conflict, which has been locked in a stalemate for months.

Last week, Trump warned Iran that the US military is “locked and loaded” and that the US was keeping an eye on Pickaxe Mountain, a facility linked to Iran’s nuclear program, for signs of activity.

“If something does not work out, I would not hesitate” to act, Trump told conservative broadcaster Hugh Hewitt on Thursday.

Yet, Trump also told reporters last week that he believed it was highly unlikely he would need to order new major strikes on Iran, declaring that the war “militarily is effectively over” after meeting with Qatar’s prime minister.

Trump also declared that the US no longer needs a deal with Tehran and told Vance – who was a chief negotiator in earlier ceasefire talks – instead to focus on the administration’s domestic anti-fraud campaign targeting Democratic-controlled cities and states.

Negotiations have stalled due to differences over Iran’s nuclear program, an issue that Trump insists be part of any deal meant to end the war. Iran wants the US first to agree to several core conditions, including lifting the naval blockade that is stopping its oil from getting to world markets.
sources.headline: Third US aircraft carrier brings thousands more troops to Middle East

sources.body:
The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command area of responsibility.

The United States has deployed a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East as diplomatic efforts to permanently end the US-Israel war on Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled.

On Monday, a US official told Al Jazeera that the USS Theodore Roosevelt had arrived in the Middle East. The aircraft carrier joins two others operating in the US Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility.

The US and Iran entered into a two-week ceasefire in April and later announced a broader memorandum of understanding in June, which collapsed in early July.

Since then, mediators from Pakistan and Qatar have been trying to prevent a return to the full-scale exchange of attacks between the US and Iran that also badly affected the broader Gulf region in March.

Last week, US President Donald Trump stated that further military strikes against Iran are “quite unlikely” and said the military component of the war was “effectively over” following discussions with Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani. But he noted the US military remains “locked and loaded” if conditions change.

Does the deployment of another aircraft carrier to the region mean the US-Israel war on Iran is going to resume?

Named after the 26th US president, Theodore Roosevelt, the vessel is a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.

Commissioned by the US Navy in 1986, the ship carries more than 5,000 personnel and a full air wing of more than 60 aircraft, including F-18s, the twin-engine, supersonic, all-weather multi-role fighter planes.

According to the US Navy, the warship is tasked with “conducting carrier air warfare operations and assisting in the planning, control, coordination and integration of air wing squadrons in support of carrier air warfare”.

Besides combat operations, the carrier also replenishes ships at sea and rescues people, including refugees, at sea.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt has performed combat and humanitarian missions since it was commissioned. During the 1990-91 Gulf War, it was deployed to the Mediterranean and the Red Sea for combat operations. In 2003, it also supported US strikes during the Iraq War.

It was also deployed in the Asia Pacific region from 2020-21 for military exercises with India, Japan, Australia, South Korea and Malaysia.

In October, a US official told Al Jazeera that the USS Theodore Roosevelt had left its San Diego base in September, bound for the Middle East. According to another official, it arrived in the Middle East on November 15 .

But the Pentagon and CENTCOM, which oversees military operations in the region, have not formally confirmed the carrier’s arrival.

The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East brings the total number of US aircraft carrier strike groups operating in the region to three. The USS George Washington and the USS George HW Bush are the other two aircraft carriers currently deployed there.

Last month, a US official told Al Jazeera that the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group (ARG), carrying more than 2,000 Marines, had also followed the USS Theodore Roosevelt to the Middle East. The Wall Street Journal reported that the strike group and naval deployments could involve an additional 9,000 to 10,000 US soldiers in total, including sailors and Marines assigned to the carrier strike group and other ships. However, the US military is yet to confirm these deployments.
sources.headline: USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East: Is the US-Iran war about to resume?

stories.headline: UK prepares closer EU ties as Burnham argues Brexit left Britain worse off

sources.body:
The prime minister has argued the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, Andy Burnham compared the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at Friday's summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

In his first major speech on foreign policy, the prime minister said that following the summit he would begin new discussions with the EU about options for "our long-term relationship".

However, he warned it would take time and insisted that "at every stage the British people will be the boss".

Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.

On the UK's current relationship with EU, Burnham said: "It's like the emperor's new clothes – where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on.

"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."

Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham set out three tests for any agreement.

Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".

He also said it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.

Finally, he said any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.

He also said the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach".

"Not adversarial. No longer burning bridges. But being constructive and positive - showing that we can come together to confront shared challenges."

Burnham said "Britain was back in the game in a big way" and would be a country that "leads with its values".

This week's summit will see the UK seek to agree further changes to former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's deal, struck in May 2025, covering fishing, trade and other areas.

The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports ahead of the meeting.

The government argues the agreement will help cut costs for businesses and could bring down prices for shoppers.

However, critics say the deal will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels, aligning with EU regulations without being able to vote on them.

Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated to EU nations.

These deals were close to being finalised under Sir Keir, with only some details still to be worked out.
sources.headline: UK lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham says ahead of EU summit

sources.body:
In Boston, Lincolnshire, a supplier of ready meals to Marks & Spencer (M&S) manufactures thousands of portions of spaghetti bolognese to be sent to the retailer's shops in the Republic of Ireland.

Every plastic pallet is meticulously individually tagged with a green-grey label “Eire”.

Every truck full of food sent to European Union countries requires hundreds of pages of forms, checks by vets, expense and delays.

It has cost M&S millions of pounds and is part of that reason the British business shut down 11 French stores in 2021.

Many smaller exporters stopped sending their goods to the EU entirely. Some produce, including sausages and certain types of seafood, were entirely stopped.

All this was the predictable consequence of former Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s 2020 deal prioritising regulatory freedom over freeflowing goods trade.

That will end with a Brexit "reset" that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to sign with the EU on Friday.

The government claims it could boost the economy to the tune of £5bn a year and cut the cost of food for households.

But will the agreement mean a return to frictionless trade for food with the EU or are there trade-offs and quid pro quos the UK will have to make?

EU affairs minister Hamish Falconer, who is a key negotiator with the bloc, acknowledged a “choice” is being made.

In exchange for being able to export produce such as Lincolnshire sausages to the 27 countries, the flipside is the extent to which the UK will be able to influence EU food policies.

The UK will have a "voice in the room", said Falconer, but no vote. Critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker", not a rule maker.

But Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules.

A Brexit reset would not involve any upfront payments, said Falconer, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment.

He said this was "reasonable" to consider what would happen if a future Conservative or Reform government wanted to undo the new arrangements. Both parties have said they would if they were in power.

"The EU is worried about that and you can see why," he said.

The BBC understands that the clause is a result of EU concerns about the possible cost of having to rebuild facilities for border food safety checks which were put in place following Brexit.

The prime minister has said he believes there is a "win-win" deal to be had with the EU.

Speaking at a Marks & Spencer food court in central London, Falconer said reducing the cost of importing food "will mean less cost for supermarkets, and I hope that less cost then turns into cheaper produce on the shelves".

He said companies have to currently deal with "pages and pages" of form-filling.

Some exports are rejected for having the wrong colour of ink on forms, or an inaccurate Latin name for cooked meats.

The reset could also mean "tearing up" checks that were introduced on goods flowing from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, following Brexit, he said, as well as separate "Not for EU" labelling.
sources.headline: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?

sources.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says UK lost more than it gained after its divorce from the bloc.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the Brexit promise failed to deliver for the United Kingdom and that the country needs to reset its relationship with the European Union to combat growing global isolationism.

During a speech at the Lord Mayor’s Banquet in London on Monday, Burnham compared the outcome of Britain’s divorce from the EU, triggered by a 2016 referendum, to the Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale “The Emperor’s New Clothes”, in which no one is willing to tell the ruler that he is, in fact, naked.

“I do try to say things as I see them,” Burnham said. “And to be frank, we have lost more than we have gained in the last 10 years. The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain.”

The remarks come ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels on Friday, which Burnham said could deliver “real improvements in people’s everyday lives in areas of the country that have felt neglected for too long”.

Any deal, he said, would have to pass three tests: it would have to be consistent with Labour’s manifesto and red lines, improve the Brexit deal to align with what people voted for in 2016 and pass his Makerfield Test, his benchmark for ensuring real improvements for people in parts of the UK that have long felt neglected.

The meeting is a key step in his pledge to reset relations with the 27-nation bloc a decade after the UK voted to leave and six years after its 2020 departure.

The UK is expected to seal a deal on trading food and drink, and make agreements on energy and emissions and a plan to let young people work for limited periods across Britain and the EU.

Burnham said the promise of the pro-Brexit campaign that Britain would “take back control” of its borders, laws and economy had not been delivered. Trade with EU countries has dropped sharply, and estimates of the economic damage range from 4 percent to 8 percent of the UK’s gross domestic product, he said.

Seeking to draw a line under a decade of political turmoil that has made him Britain’s seventh prime minister since 2016, Burnham said the UK was back on the world stage. He argued the country is well positioned to lead in an era of renewed international cooperation because of its experience since 2016.

“Brexit was the first domino to fall in a global move towards more isolationism and protectionism,” he said. “It is exactly what our enemies wanted. Russia wanted disunity within NATO and a weaker Europe.”

Burnham said that he will open a discussion with EU partners on Britain’s long-term relationship with the bloc soon after the Brussels summit. His spokesperson Tom Wells said on Monday that “no assumptions are being made” and “the British public will be the boss of any outcome”.

Until the next national election, Burnham remains bound by the pledge of Keir Starmer, whom he replaced as centre-left Labour Party leader and prime minister, not to rejoin the bloc’s tariff-free customs union or frictionless single market for goods, services and workers.
sources.headline: UK seeks closer ties with EU after Brexit fail

El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, llega al salón durante el Banquete del Lord Mayor, celebrado en el Guildhall, en Londres JUSTIN TALLIS / AFP

El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham , ha defendido este lunes que el Brexit "no ha funcionado" y ha anunciado que firmará un nuevo acuerdo con la Unión Europea (UE). El mandatario laborista ha vuelto a cargar contra la salida del Reino Unido de la UE, un proceso con el que el país "ha perdido más que ganado" , ha asegurado.

En unas declaraciones en el banquete anual del alcalde de Londres en el Guildhall de la capital, el antiguo alcalde de Manchester ha anunciado que, tras diez años en los que los "puentes con otros países se han quemado", a partir de ahora Reino Unido va a resetear sus relaciones internacionales : "El mundo ha cambiado desde 2016. Parecía muy fácil ir por nuestra cuenta. Ahora no es así" .

El próximo 20 de noviembre tendrá lugar la esperada cumbre entre la UE y el Reino Unido en Berlín , en la que se abordarán cuestiones de defensa y seguridad, comercio, relajación de controles fronterizos o la movilización de estudiantes. Aunque el primer ministro no ha dado detalles concretos sobre el contenido del acuerdo, ha señalado que este deberá ser coherente con el manifiesto laborista y las líneas del Gobierno y mejorar el acuerdo anterior del Brexit, más próximo a lo que la gente pensaba que votaba en 2016.

Según The Guardian, que ha adelantado los fragmentos del discruso relativos a política internacional, Burnham pretende firmar acuerdos que podrían aumentar el PIB en un 0,4% — unas 17.000 millones de libras — en materia de agricultura, comercio de emisiones y un programa de juventud.

El primer ministro britántico no ha dudado en comparar el debate sobre el Brexit con el tradicional cuento infantil de El traje nuevo del emperador , en el que ningún ciudadano se atrevía a decirle al monarca que estaba desnudo: "Es incómodo, pero tenemos que tener esta conversación".

También ha hecho mención a la posición que va a mantener su Gobierno en Oriente Medio, donde apoyará la solución de "dos estados" entre Palestina e Israel y exigirá que Irán no tenga un arma nuclear, sin que ello suponga una guerra que "dure eternamente". También ha fijado su postura respecto a la guerra de Ucrania, el conflicto que, considera, ha sido el primer paso para el acercamiento con los países de la Unión. "Hemos trabajado bien con los compañeros europeos. Apoyando al más pequeño sin esperar nada a cambio, representa nuestros valores. Seguiremos apoyando a Ucrania ".

Han pasado 10 años desde que los británicos votaron a favor de abandonar la UE. Una década marcada por la inestabilidad política , un débil crecimiento económico y un eterno debate entre la vinculación con los vecinos europeos. El flirteo de Burnham con la Unión Europea se encuentra con escépticos incluso dentro de su propio partido, lo que evidencia la división que vive todo el Reino Unido sobre esta cuestión.

Desde su llegada al Ejecutivo, el conocido como Rey del Norte , por su etapa como alcalde de Manchester, ha coqueteado en varias ocasiones con la idea de una vuelta a la UE. El pasado mes de septiembre, en una entrevista con la BBC, admitió que el Brexit había causado " más daño que beneficio ". Anteriormente, en la conferencia anual del Partido Laborista, aseguró que no darían a Gran Bretaña "un rumbo claro hasta decidir cuál es la relación a largo plazo con la UE".

stories.headline: California sues OpenAI over alleged failures to safeguard models linked to cyberattacks

sources.body:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the ChatGPT-maker misled and endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence (AI) models without proper safeguards.

In the lawsuit, Bonta cited the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face by experimental OpenAI agents which accessed the internet to breach that company's internal systems.

Bonta claimed OpenAI created a public nuisance and violated the state's unfair competition laws.

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told the BBC in a statement that Bonta's lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab".

Other major AI developers including Anthropic, Meta, and Google have also said their models have staged similar attacks.

But Bonta's lawsuit, filed in San Francisco, where the company is headquartered, appears to be the first such suit filed by a US state.

Hundreds of OpenAI agents coordinated the Hugging Face attack over two days even though they were supposed to be contained in a safe testing environment.

The incident drew added scrutiny because the agents went as far as attempting to cover their tracks.

Bonta announced an investigation into the incident in September, and served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI as part of its probe.

"The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it - this disregard for public safety violated California law," Bonta said in a statement on Monday.

OpenAI said it has been transparent and responsive to the Attorney General's office.

"We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged - and will continue to engage - constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry," the company said.

The company added that, since the Hugging Face incident, it has worked to understand and address "misaligned model activity" which industry figures often refer to as rogue agents.

Nathan Calvin, chief strategy officer at AI safety campaign group Encode AI, said the lawsuit "recognises something we at Encode have long raised alarms about".

"OpenAI and other companies developing frontier AI systems have safety and security practices that are insufficient to protect the public from risks that could be catastrophic," he said.

stories.headline: US tightens export rules to block China's remote access to advanced AI chips

sources.body:
Trump administration introduces export licence requirements for Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil.

United States President Donald Trump’s administration has announced new restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips amid fallout from the alleged spy scandal involving AI giant Nvidia.

The rule announced by the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) on Monday aims to prevent Chinese AI developers from getting around export controls by remotely accessing data centres in third countries, particularly in Southeast Asia.

It designates Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil as countries with an “unacceptable risk of diversion” and requires anyone seeking to export advanced chips to those destinations to obtain an export licence.

BIS, which sits under the Department of Commerce, said the change was a “logical extension” of the existing requirement for companies to obtain a licence to export or transfer chips to firms based in China.

“The United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the global adoption of American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring that sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten US national security,” BIS said in a statement.

The restrictions come as Nvidia’s export of advanced chips is under scrutiny following claims that former CEO Jensen Huang was romantically involved with a woman recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security for espionage.

Huang, who became one of the most prominent faces of the AI boom at the helm of Nvidia, resigned last week amid a company board investigation into allegations involving the Chinese-born executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.

Beijing has denied the spying allegations, made by unnamed US officials in media reports, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive identified as Jensen Huang’s ex-romantic partner, has not publicly commented on the claims.

Late Monday, the US commerce and justice departments said for the first time that investigators had opened a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.

The Commerce Department began investigating Megaspeed for potential export control violations in 2024, leading BIS officials to conduct an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and to interview Alice Huang the following year, the statement said.

The Department of Justice subsequently took the “lead role” in the criminal investigation, according to the statement.

“The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred,” it said.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Monday as investors weighed the scandal’s fallout on the AI rollout.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49 percent, closing in the red for the third consecutive session.

sources.headline: Chase Bank says operations are back to normal after ‘bug’ disrupts transactions

sources.body: American users of several major banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.
sources.headline: Chase outage disrupts online banking and Zelle payments in United States

sources.body:
Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services.

Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was "temporary" and not "systemic" or "cyber-related".

Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening.

The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems, including a massive Microsoft outage , a network failure that grounded all US flights , and United Airlines reporting a "widespread system outage".

Problems started on Monday afternoon. There were almost 5,000 reports of problems with Chase Bank's services, according to the Downdetector website.

Clients reported issues accessing their online accounts, viewing balances and performing transactions, like bank transfers and wire transfers, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

A Chase Bank customer in Texas told the outlet that he could not deposit a check at a Dallas branch on Monday, reporting that he was told his transaction could not be completed. He said a bank teller told the customer in front of him that the "system was down" but did not provide additional details.

Chase Bank told its customers that "some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete" but they still had "access to their accounts and funds".

The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company's webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US.

The exact nature of the bug was unclear. The BBC has contacted Chase Bank.

Bank of America customers had issues at ATMs and using mobile banking services online, while US Bank customers reported issues with their online accounts and the bank's mobile app, CBS reported.

Customers using another institution, US Bank, also reported issues transferring funds and Wells Fargo customers said they had problems signing into their accounts, getting account balances and making transactions.

US Bank said some its systems were not directly affected but clients using the Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent.

Zelle has said its service is "operating as it should" and issues at other banks could be affecting payments.

Customers also reported issues with Truist, PNC and Capital One but all these companies told the BBC they have not been impacted.

As of 18:00 EST (23:00 GMT), Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a fall in the number of reported outages.

Just as the banking issue affected US customers on Monday, United Airlines confirmed a "widespread system outage", which it described as "a technology issue affecting departing flights".

The Chicago-based airline did not say what is believed to have caused the issue, but a spokesperson said it is not related to cybersecurity.

Un informe del CNI fechado el 11 de noviembre y remitido a la Audiencia Nacional determina que no ha hallado evidencias de que la entrada masiva de más de 80.000 migrantes los días 30 y 31 de julio en Ceuta fuera "instigada, planeada o coordinada" por Marruecos. Por su parte, la Guardia Civil descarta que el informe del Centro Nacional de Inteligencia del 29 de julio, un día antes de la crisis, fuera "un aviso o alerta temprana" de la misma.

En un escrito al que ha tenido acceso Rtve Noticias presentado a la magistrada de la Audiencia Nacional María Tardón, que investiga la entrada masiva de migrantes a Ceuta, el CNI señala que "hasta donde se sabe en estos momentos, l a movilización fue el producto de un lIamamiento en redes sociales en el que no puede reconocerse la existencia de un único dinamizador, ni la vinculación de los que fueron detectados con el aparato del estado marroquí".

"Tras las investigaciones en profundidad realizadas por el CNI, no se han encontrado evidencias que permitan afirmar que organismos estatales marroquíes estén implicados en el diseño, puesta en marcha o coordinación de una acción con intenciones deliberadamente agresivas de este tipo contra España", destaca.

Para el servicio secreto español, una cuestión diferente es "el conocimiento que, efectivamente, tenían las autoridades marroquíes de la existencia de convocatorias con un alcance masivo animando a entrar en Ceuta, y las decisiones que tomaron antes y durante el suceso, en las que priorizaron la seguridad de la celebración de la Fiesta del Trono que se celebraba, con asistencia del rey Mohamed VI, en el cercano palacio real de Rincón".

Los agentes indican a la jueza que, según la información obtenida, las decisiones adoptadas por Marruecos "tuvieron como consecuencia la entrada de personas de manera incontrolada en la ciudad autónoma sin que encontraran oposición eficaz por parte de las autoridades marroquíes".

El organismo de inteligencia sí que ha detectado, "en cambio", la actividad de una serie de dinamizadores en el ámbito de las redes sociales que "han actuado de forma descentralizada, múltiple, autogestionada y colaborativa en la difusión de la convocatoria de entrada en Ceuta". Pero recalca que no se ha observado "una estructura organizativa de dirección o coordinación centralizada" que hiciera los primeros lamamientos ni los amplificara después.

Y concluye que "no se ha establecido que existiera una acción concertada por parte de organismos estatales marroquíes que permita hablar de una integración de los dinamizadores en estructuras superiores para la ejecución de una acción deliberada en perjuicio de los intereses españoles".

También este lunes se ha conocido otro documento de la Guardia Civil, fechado también el 11 de noviembre, en el que descarta que el informe del CNI del 29 de julio, un día antes de que empezara la entrada masiva a Ceuta, fuera un "aviso o alerta temprana" de la crisis.

Cabe recordar que el informe del CNI de esa fecha fue usado de ariete político contra el Gobierno, al que se le ha acusado de conocer lo que iba a ocurrir antes de que sucediera, y que la crisis se saldó con la dimisión el pasado 11 de septiembre del jefe de gabinete del delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Gonzalo Sanz, tras insistir en que trasladó la información de los servicios secretos a su superior.

El derecho a la vivienda ha centrado el acto que esta tarde ha protagonizado la candidata de Frente Amplio a la presidencia del Gobierno, Ada Colau , que desde Madrid ha asegurado que "la lucha contra la extrema derecha y la lucha por el derecho a la vivienda son dos caras de la misma moneda". Respondía así a la afirmación de Pedro Sánchez , que dijo que le gustaría gobernar con la exalcaldesa de Barcelona y la formación que representa: " Para que el Frente Amplio esté en un futuro Consejo de Ministros de un gobierno progresista, el primer decreto que debe aprobar es el que estabilice los precios del alquiler y baje los precios de los contratos ".

Colau se ha mostrado rotunda al asegurar que "el bipartidismo es responsable directo de que la vivienda se haya convertido en una mercancía y no en un derecho como dice la Constitución". "Hay un poder inmobiliario en nuestro país con el que el bipartidismo ha tenido una cierta relación de complicidad", ha asegurado, mirando hacia el Partido Popular, pero también hacia el Ejecutivo socialista: "Estos años en que se ha acentuado la crisis de la vivienda el PSOE no ha regulado como se le estaba pidiendo por parte de otros partidos políticos y la calle".

Según ha explicado, "el bipartidismo ha podido hacer estas políticas de mercantilización de vivienda utilizando la idea de defender a los propietarios". "Basta ya con esta mentira. Nosotros defendemos a la mayoría social , que son los pequeños propietarios y las personas inquilinas", ha reclamado tras cargar contra una legislación "antipersonas", que "atenta contra derechos humanos" de esa mayoría, condicionando los proyectos de vida de los ciudadanos: "Esto tiene que terminar".

Colau, que ha participado en la grabación de un podcast junto a la portavoz de Más Madrid, Rita Maestre , y la abogada Alejandra Jacinto , ha recordado el compromiso que Sánchez adquirió con ella públicamente para regular los alquileres en 2019: "Si se hubiera hecho la historia sería bastante distinta", ha asegurado.

Yolanda Díaz , que este lunes ha sido noticia tras retirar su candidatura para liderar la Organización Internacional de Trabajo (OIT), ha acudido al acto de Colau, donde sido recibida con aplausos y el público en pie. Las primera palabras de la candidata de Frente Amplio han sido para agradecer la presencia de la vicepresidenta primera y ministra del ala de Sumar en el Ejecutivo de coalición: "Algún día la OIT se dará cuenta del gran error que ha cometido renunciando a la mejor ministra de trabajo que ha habido", le ha dicho.

La candidata ha explicado lo que significa el lema de su campaña: "Un voto como una casa es decir basta", ha señalado, antes de advertir que " hay que cambiar el paradigma ": "Ya no nos sirven pequeñas medidas, ayudas, parches... Es muy propio del PSOE permitir la especulación por un lado y por otro decir que da ayudas a los jóvenes. Ya no nos sirve", ha reclamado, para pedir un cambio legislativo real.

stories.headline: Government plans to approve public sector pay rises during the election campaign

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, 

El Gobierno aprobará mañana la subida de sueldo a los funcionarios correspondiente a 2027, según ha anunciado el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en una entrevista en Telecinco. El Gobierno se había comprometido a aprobar esta subida, pactada en noviembre de 2025, en los Consejos de Ministros que restaban antes de las elecciones del 29 de noviembre.

La subida acordada implica un aumento del 4,5% del sueldo para 2027 pero el Gobierno tiene que aprobar también un 0,5% adicional de subida correspondiente a este año en curso, vinculado a la subida del IPC. Es decir, en términos agregados, el salario de los funcionarios subirá un 5% el año que viene.

”Estamos hablando de cinco millones de trabajadores y trabajadoras que se van a beneficiar de este aumento de la capacidad salarial”, ha explicado el presidente en una entrevista.

Gobierno y sindicatos acordaron hace un año, y al margen de los Presupuestos -prorrogados desde 2023-, una subida salarial global para los empleados públicos del 11% para el periodo 2025-2028. El objetivo era compensar la pérdida de poder adquisitivo después de que el año pasado, los funcionarios pasaran casi todo el ejercicio sin actualizar sus retribuciones. El acuerdo incluyó también compromisos para modernizar la Administración y mejorar las condiciones laborales de sus plantillas.

Ese total del 11% se distribuye en un alza del 2,5% para 2025, ya consolidada, otra del 1,5% para 2026, al que hay que sumar el 0,5% adicional que se pactó si el IPC medio anual supera el 1,5% (algo que ocurrirá), una subida del 4,5% para 2027 y, por último, una del 2% para 2028.

Al conocerse que se aprobaría este aumento, el sindicato CSIF recordó que había reclamado la subida antes de las elecciones para evitar retrasos por las limitaciones que tiene el Ejecutivo cuando entra en funciones. Añadieron también que supervisarán que las distintas administraciones, estatales, autonómicas y locales, puedan presupuestar y preparar nóminas con criterios homogéneos.

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez , ha anunciado que el Consejo de Ministros de este martes aprobará la subida del sueldo de los trabajadores públicos para el año 2027 . La subida del salario de funcionarios y empleados públicos será del 4,5% en 2027, según el compromiso alcanzado el pasado 20 de octubre entre el Gobierno y los sindicatos CCOO, UGT y CSIF. En las últimas semanas y ya en plena precampaña electoral (ahora ya campaña), el Ejecutivo ha ido aprobando medidas sociales en consejos de ministros ordinarios e incluso extraordinarios. Moncloa quiere que estas medidas sean un adelanto de lo que podría hacer la próxima legislatura si Sánchez revalida el Gobierno. La oposición , por su parte, le acusa de adoptar medidas electoralistas para sacar rédito electoral.

Sánchez ha explicado en una entrevista en Telecinco que de esta medida se beneficiarán todos los empleados públicos, que "mejorarán su capacidad adquisitiva". El líder socialista ha asegurado que su partido defiende "una España que avance y que progrese" y como ejemplo de ellos ha puesto que el Ejecutivo ha aprobado "avances en el ámbito del poder adquisitivo" . Acto seguido ha citado los dos más recientes: la subida del salario mínimo interprofesional anunciada este lunes (en ocho años ha subido un 66%) y el alza del sueldo de los trabajadores públicos que se aprobará este martes. En total, de estas dos medidas se beneficiarán cinco millones de personas.

Si a ello se suma la revalorización de las pensiones que habrá conforme al IPC, ha añadido que los ciudadanos que verán incrementada directamente su capacidad adquisitiva gracias a sus políticas serán unos 15 millones de personas .

En cuanto a la crisis de Ceuta , el jefe del Ejecutivo ha reconocido que "siempre se podría haber reaccionado antes" . Pero a pesar de ello, ha puesto en valor que el Gobierno "actuó desde el primer día después de la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo" y que algunas medidas, como la prolongación del espigón del Tarajal con boyas "ya estaban previstas" antes de la avalancha.

Según ha explicado, "el Gobierno llevaba días trabajando con Marruecos para proteger la frontera" , pero que finalmente no pudo evitar la entrada masiva de decenas de miles de migrantes irregulares.

Durante la entrevista, Sánchez ha respondido por la crisis de Ceuta, por la dimisión del ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, o por la llegada masiva de inmigrantes a Canarias de las últimas semanas. A este respecto, ha querido poner en valor los datos globales de llegada de migrantes, no los datos puntuales de la entrada masiva en Ceuta o de la llegada de migrantes a la isla de El Hierro. En este sentido, ha dicho que este año "ha bajado la llegada de inmigrantes irregulares un 38%" . Y que en El Hierro, sin contar los datos de estas últimas semanas, había caído "más de un 70%".

El presentador, Carlos Franganillo, ha puesto de relieve que la política de inmigración del Gobierno de España es casi única en Europa y que va en contra de lo que defiende la gran mayoría de los países. "¿Se siente usted un conductor kamikaze por ir en la dirección contraria de los demás?", le ha dicho. Sánchez ha respondido que no: "Me siento como una persona con principios de un país grande que respeta los derechos humanos".

En plena campanya electoral, el president del govern espanyol, Pedro Sánchez , ha anunciat que el Consell de Ministres aprovarà aquest dimarts l'augment del 4,5% del sou als treballadors públics per a l'any que ve.

El candidat socialista a les eleccions generals ha fet aquest anunci en una entrevista a Telecinco aquest dilluns a la nit.

"Aquest dimarts cinc milions de treballadors es veuran beneficiats d'aquest compromís del govern d'Espanya d'augmentar la capacitat salarial", ha afirmat. Sánchez ha subratllat que "els que cobren el salari mínim interprofessional i els de la funció pública, veuran com el seu poder adquisitiu augmenta per sobre de la inflació", recordant que en la reunió d'aquest dimarts el govern espanyol també aprovarà la pujada del salari mínim interprofessional per al 2027 en un 5,3%.

L'increment salarial del 4,5% per al 2027 ja estava pactat entre la Moncloa i els sindicats CCOO, UGT i CSIF en l'acord signat el novembre del 2025, que preveia una pujada acumulada de l'11% entre el 2025 i el 2028.

L'executiu de Pedro Sánchez ja havia garantit als sindicats que aplicaria l'augment amb efectes de l'1 de gener del 2027, però fins ara no n'havia concretat la data d'aprovació. La mesura beneficiarà més de tres milions d'empleats públics .

D'altra banda, el Consell de Ministres també donarà llum verda a un sou mínim que quedarà en 1.286 euros bruts al mes , 65 euros més que l'actual.

Poques hores després de renunciar a la candidatura per dirigir l'Organització Internacional del Treball (OIT), la vicepresidenta primera i ministra de Treball, Yolanda Díaz , ha fet l'anunci de la pujada de l'SMI, que quedarà en 18.004 euros anuals en 14 pagues .

En declaracions a La Sexta, Díaz ha aclarit que l'increment per al 2027 no suposarà que aquest salari comenci a tributar en l'IRPF . "No pagaran impostos", insistia sobre els treballadors que el perceben.

Díaz defensa que el salari mínim és "la millor eina per reduir la pobresa laboral i atacar-la".

De tota manera, aquesta serà la primera vegada que el govern espanyol tira endavant una pujada de l'SMI sense el suport dels sindicats, que demanaven un 7% de pujada . Tampoc té el vistiplau de la patronal. La CEOE demanava que fos el govern que surti de les eleccions del 29 de novembre qui ho negociés.

De fet, el 5,3% d'increment és superior al que va fixar la proposta del comitè d'experts del ministeri que dirigeix Díaz, del 4,9% , que equival a la variació de l'IPC de l'últim mes a escala estatal.

Des del Ministeri de Treball –que estima que el sou mínim afectarà uns dos milions i mig de treballadors –, defensen que l'increment de l'SMI el deixa al llindar del 60% del salari mitjà espanyol, tal com recomana la Carta Social Europea.

En els últims deu anys, l'SMI ha crescut en més de 500 euros al mes . Dels 707,60 euros del 2017 als 1.286 del 2027, ha registrat una pujada del 81%, significativament superior a la del salari mitjà.

Aglomeraciones en la estación de Sants por los retrasos en el primer de huelga de Rodalies en Renfe, el pasado martes 12. / JORDI OTIX / PIM

La normalidad seguirá sin llegar a Rodalies un día más. Este martes, el conjunto del sector ferroviario español va a la huelga para reclamar, por cuarta vez en tres semanas, una mejora de las condiciones de seguridad para los maquinistas . Operarán bajo servicios mínimos todas las redes de Cercanías del Estado, todos los trenes de alta velocidad --AVE, Iryo y Ouigo--, los de media distancia e incluso las empresas de transporte de mercancías estarán llamadas al parón sindical de mañana. En Catalunya , fuentes de Rodalies ya apuntan que la jornada "puede ser muy complicada" y animan a los usuarios a buscar alternativas de transporte ante la posibilidad de que, tal y como pasó hace una semana, los sindicatos no cumplan los servicios mínimos establecidos.

El Departament d'Empresa i Treball estipuló estos servicios mínimos de Rodalies en un 66% en hora punta --entre las 06.00 y las 09.30 horas y entre las 17.00 y las 20.30 horas-- y un 33% el resto de la jornada . En AVE y Larga Distancia, los servicios mínimos serán del 72% . Los precedentes de estas semanas no auguran un día fácil.

El 29 de octubre, un día después del accidente de Urda (Toledo), el Sindicato Español de Maquinistas y Ayudantes Ferroviarios (SEMAF) sí cumplió con los servicios mínimos, y la jornada se desarrolló sin grandes problemas . En cambio, la semana pasada, tanto el martes 10 como el miércoles 11, gran parte de los maquinistas no obedeciero n las órdenes de la cúpula y dejaron sin servicio a los pocos trenes que estaban programados para aquellos días. La Generalitat activó esos días un refuerzo de 95 autobuses de las principales líneas interurbanas que caen bajo su titularidad, pero no pudieron evitar que muchos de los más de 400.000 usuarios que utilizan cada día la red de Rodalies llegaran con graves retrasos a su destino habitual. La semana pasada, según datos de Adif recopilados por los usuarios en el portal 'retards.cat', se cancelaron más de 1.600 trenes y los retrasos de aquellos que sí circularon fueron, de media, de más de 40 minutos .

Todos los sindicatos del sector se han manifestado ya este lunes frente a las puertas del Congreso en Madrid . Allí, han puesto sobre la mesa las reclamaciones que, a su parecer, hacen necesario el paro sindical de 24 horas , justo 20 días después del accidente de alta velocidad en Urda que dejó 69 muertos .

En conjunto, denuncian que "el modelo de ferrocarril actual ha fallado" . Pau Mercè, coordinador del sector ferroviario de CCOO en Catalunya, asegura que "las diferentes externalizaciones de la actividad han provocado falta de personal, de mantenimiento y problemas de seguridad" y denuncia que las responsabilidades ante los incidentes "deberían ser políticas e institucionales y no de las personas trabajadoras". "Exigimos un ferrocarril público, de calidad y seguro" , zanja.

Son reclamaciones que comparten también UGT, Alferro, la CGT, el Sindicato Ferroviario y el SEMAF . Todos ellos han llamado este martes a la huelga a sus trabajadores. Además de estas reclamaciones, en el sector ha sentado especialmente mal el tratamiento que el ya exministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente , hizo del accidente de Urda. El Comité General de Renfe denunció tras el accidente las filtraciones de las grabaciones de las llamadas entre las cabinas del Iryo y el AVE siniestrados con el centro de control de Adif en Atocha y criticó que se señalara "al eslabón más débil de la cadena".

El sector ferroviari manté el pols amb el Ministeri de Transports per reclamar mesures de seguretat arran de l' accident d'Urda (Toledo) a finals d'octubre, i els que hi va haver al gener a Adamuz (Còrdova) i a Gelida , a l'Alt Penedès.

Aquest dimarts hi ha convocada una vaga per part dels comitès d'empresa de Renfe i Adif, que s'ha fet extensiva a les altres operadores ferroviàries de passatgers i mercaderies. Com a prèvia, diversos sindicats han fet una concentració aquest dilluns a Madrid .

L'última reunió entre sindicats i Transports, divendres passat, va permetre alguns "avenços tècnics" en les reivindicacions, segons el sindicat de maquinistes Semaf, però els sindicats volen veure les mesures aprovades i publicades abans de desconvocar cap aturada.

Entre els avenços, l'Agència Estatal de Seguretat Ferroviària ha publicat una guia sobre com actuar si falla el sistema de seguretat LZB que recomana reprendre la circulació amb "marxa a la vista", a diferència de l'ordre que va rebre l'AVE accidentat a Urda.

En el calendari de vagues es manté per al 23 de novembre l'aturada que Semaf tenia prevista per al dia 12 amb la voluntat de "facilitar la negociació sense aixecar la pressió".

Les protestes d'aquest dilluns i la vaga de dimarts arriben després que aquest cap de setmana, a Madrid, un maquinista hagi resultat ferit lleu arran d'un despreniment que va fer descarrilar la locomotora d'un tren de mercaderies .

Algunes de les mesures que hi ha encara en negociació s'arrosseguen de l'acord que sindicats i el Ministeri de Transports van acordar al febrer després dels accidents d'Adamuz i Gelida i que llavors va permetre desconvocar unes aturades.

És el cas d'un protocol d'actuació davant de fenòmens meteorològics adversos. Els sindicats volen criteris clars per saber què passa amb la circulació de trens quan s'envia un ES-Alert als mòbils i es demana a la població limitar la mobilitat.

Entre les exigències hi ha que l'Agència Estatal de Meteorologia emeti alertes específiques per al sector ferroviari, així com criteris homogenis per a les diferents empreses del sector.

L'accident ferroviari d'Urda ha accelerat les negociacions per la seguretat dels trens. Quines mesures reclamen els maquinistes? Ens ho explica @marc_garciab, periodista de 3CatInfo https://t.co/sbG7SXI1Q0 https://t.co/yCCuYFbyAk

Una altra de les reivindicacions dels sindicats és modificar el reial decret de seguretat ferroviària per fixar quin temps màxim han de treballar de forma continuada els controladors de trànsit ferroviari .

La proposta que hi ha sobre la taula estableix un màxim de dues hores continuades amb una pausa de 30 minuts . Segons apunten alguns sindicats, la intenció de Transports és portar aquests canvis a aprovació al Consell de Ministres d'aquest dimarts.

Els representants dels treballadors avisen també que per tirar endavant aquesta modificació i garantir els temps de descansos caldrà un augment de plantilla .

Entre les peticions dels sindicats també hi ha la de fer un seguiment efectiu de les limitacions temporals de velocitat per planificar obres de reparació o un registre únic per comunicar riscos de la infraestructura supervisat per l'Agència Estatal de Seguretat Ferroviària.

Imagen de la concentración de ayer en Sant Jaume en defensa de una vivienda digna

La Guardia Urbana desalojó entrada ya la madrugada de hoy a unas 250 personas que se habían se concentrado la plaza Sant Jaume para protestar por el desalojo “a traición” que la madrugada de ayer puso punto final a la acampada de plaza Catalunya.

Seis activistas anunciaron su intención de iniciar una huelga de hambre para forzar una mesa de negociación en la que estén sentados, además de los colectivos en defensa de la vivienda, el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona y el Govern.

“El Consistorio quiere que nuestra reivindicación salga del foco mediático”, se quejaba una portavoz. También anunciaron su intención de pernoctar en Sant Jaume y de volver a la Barceloneta, donde un reducido grupo pasó la noche del domingo.

El Ayuntamiento no lo permitió en una operación que se saldó sin incidentes.
sources.headline: La Guardia Urbana también desaloja a los concentrados en la plaza Sant Jaume

A pie de calle | Desalojo de la acampada de plaza de Catalunya de madrugada / JORDI OTIX / VÍDEO: G. SÁNCHEZ / J. OTIX / M. TUDELA

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona desalojó este lunes de madrugada la acampada de la plaza de Catalunya , que llevaba 47 días instalada en este céntrico espacio de la capital catalana.

La intervención ha puesto fin a una protesta iniciada el pasado 29 de septiembre para reivindicar el derecho a la vivienda tras el desahucio y fallecimiento de Maricarmen Abascal en Madrid . Este martes se ha desalojado de la plaza de Sant Jaume las personas que se habían instalado tras ser el fin de la acampada de plaza de Catalunya.

Sigue en este directo todas las novedades y las reacciones al desalojo.

Poco antes de las doce, la Guardia Urbana ha entrado con furgonetas en plaza Sant Jaume, y han bajado antidisturbios del cuerpo de seguridad municipal. Los agentes han formado una línea y han empezado a avanzar hacia el primer grupo formado por la treintena de activistas, acompañándolos hacia fuera de la plaza por la calle Sant Jaume hasta llegar al metro de Via Laietana, donde se han acabado de dispersar. Toda la acción ha sido pacífica, aunque mientras recogían sus pertenencias, los activistas llamaban "vergüenza".

La Guardia Urbana de Barcelona ha desalojado sobre las 00.00 de la plaza Sant Jaume la cuarentena de activistas que seguían concentrados en este lugar para criticar el desmantelamiento del campamento de plaza Catalunya, incluidos los seis que habían comenzado una huelga de hambre. A partir de las siete de la tarde, unas 250 personas según el consistorio se concentraron ante el Ayuntamiento, ya las nueve se hizo una asamblea en la que las seis personas decidieron esta medida y otro grupo acordó quedarse a dormir, sin parar tiendas. La Guardia Urbana les ha desalojado a todos en dos fases tres horas más tarde, primero la treintena y posteriormente los seis. Ambas actuaciones se han hecho sin incidentes, pero la segunda con mayor tensión.

Esquerra Republicana ha anunciado que revisará la actuación de la Guardia Urbana durante el desalojo de plaza de Catalunya. Su portavoz adjunto en el Ayuntamiento, Jordi Coronas , ha puesto el foco en la situación de las personas sin hogar que dormían en la acampada y que ahora deben buscar otro lugar donde pasar la noche.

Coronas ha asegurado que velarán para que reciban " el acompañamiento necesario" y ha reclamado al gobierno municipal que les ofrezca alternativas de alojamiento para evitar que tengan que volver a la calle.

La acampada de plaza de Catalunya ya es historia después de 47 días de protesta por el derecho a la vivienda . La Guardia Urbana, con el apoyo de los Mossos d'Esquadra, ha desalojado esta madrugada a 295 personas y retirado 150 tiendas de campaña. Los servicios municipales han trabajado en la limpieza de la plaza, de donde se han retirado 45 toneladas de residuos.

Mientras tanto, unas 70 personas se han trasladado al Espigó del Gas, en la Barceloneta , para continuar la acampada. El Ayuntamiento ha anunciado que seguirá de cerca los movimientos de los desalojados y las posibles nuevas ocupaciones del espacio público.

sources.body: 250 persones s’han concentrat aquest dilluns a la tarda a la plaça de Sant Jaume per protestar contra l’actuació policial que ha desallotjat l’acampada prohabitatge que hi havia instal·lada a plaça de Catalunya. Segons els organitzadors de la concentració, sis dels activistes de l’antiga acampada volen començar una vaga de fam i acampar a la plaça de Sant Jaume . Els organitzadors de l’acampada expliquen que han volgut establir, sense èxit, una taula de diàleg amb les administracions per trobar una alternativa d’habitatge per als acampats sense llar o que estan en situació de risc de vulnerabilitat. En aquesta línia, l’acampada denuncia com aquestes solucions no han arribat i que, per aquest motiu, s’ha decidit iniciar la vaga de fam. També et pot interessar Una part de l’acampada de l’habitatge es trasllada a la platja de la Barceloneta Andrea Muñoz Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura Neteja de la plaça de Catalunya Pel que fa a la plaça de Catalunya , els equips de neteja municipal continuen fent tasques de desinfecció de tot l’espai. Per aquest motiu, l’emblemàtica plaça està acordonada i resta tancada al públic aquest dilluns a la tarda. Després del desallotjament d’aquesta matinada, hi han treballat 27 equips de neteja i 55 operaris municipals. Segons l’Ajuntament, les tasques de retirada i neteja de l’espai han recollit un total de 45 tones de residus. També et pot interessar Collboni defensa el desallotjament de l’acampada per garantir la convivència, seguretat i salubritat Marina Sancho 1 minut de lectura
